passage: In the Land of Shapes, architects build structures using strict geometric rules. A regular hexagon has six sides, and its interior angle sum is calculated by multiplying the number of triangles formed by diagonals, which is four, by 180 degrees. Unlike a simple triangle, a polygon with more sides always has a larger interior angle sum. Architects often use a rhombus for floor tiles, knowing its diagonals are not equal, though they do bisect each other at right angles. For window frames, they use a rectangle, which has equal diagonals that do not meet at 90 degrees. When designing a bridge, they place a support beam exactly halfway between two sides of a triangle; this segment is always half the length of the third side it is parallel to. Finally, they define a trapezium as a shape with exactly one pair of parallel sides, ensuring no confusion with parallelograms that possess two pairs. Every shape must follow these laws to remain stable in the Land of Shapes.

items.q: An architect finds the interior angle sum of a regular hexagon using diagonals. What is it?
items.explain: Diagonals split a hexagon into four triangles, and 4 × 180 = 720 degrees.
